prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury attorney in Chicago for a car accident claim?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” Chicago attorney for every car-accident claim — the right lawyer depends on your injuries, the facts, insurance issues, and whether you’ll likely need to go to trial. That said, you can find excellent representation by focusing on experienced plaintiff trial lawyers who handle serious auto-crash cases. Below I’ll give practical guidance, some highly regarded firms to consider, and how to choose the right lawyer for your case.

Well-regarded Chicago plaintiff firms (examples)
- Clifford Law Offices
- Levin & Perconti
- Corboy & Demetrio
- Salvi, Schostok & Pritchard
- Power Rogers (plaintiff-focused)
These firms are frequently listed in local and national legal rankings and have strong records in car-crash and catastrophic-injury litigation. This is not an exhaustive list and not an endorsement — it’s a starting point.

How to pick the right attorney
- Relevant experience: Ask about experience with car-accident cases similar to yours (same injury types, fault/insurance issues).  
- Trial record: Prefer lawyers who actually try cases to juries (not just settle). Look for verdicts and settlements in comparable matters.  
- Resources: Serious crash cases often need medical experts, accident reconstruction, and cash up-front. Make sure the firm has those resources.  
- Communication: Ask how often you’ll get updates and who your day-to-day contact will be.  
- Fees: Most personal-injury lawyers work on contingency (no fee unless you recover). Ask the exact percentage, who pays costs, and how fees change if you sue or go to trial.  
- Local experience: Lawyers familiar with Cook County judges, prosecutors (if criminal issues), and local hospitals can be an advantage.  
- Client references and reviews: Check Google, Avvo, Martindale-Hubbell, Super Lawyers, and Better Business Bureau.

Questions to ask in a free consultation
- How many car-accident cases have you handled? How many reached trial?  
- Have you handled cases with injuries like mine? (provide specifics)  
- What’s a realistic settlement range for a case like mine?  
- Who will handle my case day-to-day?  
- How do you charge (contingency %, costs)?  
- Can you provide references or recent verdicts/settlements?

Red flags
- Pressure to sign immediately.  
- No contingency fee or unwillingness to put fee agreement in writing.  
- Poor reviews describing communication breakdowns.  
- Reluctance to take cases to trial if appropriate.

Practical next steps now
1. Get medical treatment and keep records.  
2. Preserve evidence: police report, photos, witness contacts, medical bills.  
3. Avoid giving recorded statements to the other insurer without a lawyer.  
4. Contact 3–4 firms for free consultations and compare answers, fees, and comfort level.  
5. Act quickly — Illinois generally has a 2-year statute of limitations for personal injury claims (and much shorter notice rules for claims against government entities), so don’t wait.

If you’d like, tell me a few details (zip code, severity of injuries, whether the other driver was at fault or uninsured, whether there were any police tickets or DUIs) and I’ll help shortlist 3–5 local lawyers or firms that fit your situation.
